outcome: Since 26 January 2024, several genuine cases of the Gan-Gross-Prasad (GGP) conjecture — which is really a family of restriction/period statements across group types — have been settled by conventional (non-AI) mathematics: most notably a three-paper series (Boisseau-Lu-Xue, arXiv:2404.07342, 2601.01727, 2601.01738; April 2024 to January 2026) completing the proof of the global GGP conjecture and its Ichino-Ikeda refinement for Fourier-Jacobi periods on unitary groups, and a combination of two 2025 papers (Chen-Chen arXiv:2507.04355, building on prior work of P. Boisseau) settling the non-tempered local GGP conjecture for Archimedean general linear groups. A separate item the triage flagged — the (U(2n),U(1)) case and its refinement, published in Mathematische Annalen in October 2024 — is a case of predates-the-window work: the arXiv preprint (2205.09471) was first posted 19 May 2022, and the 2024 event was only the journal's online publication, which per the dating rule does not count. No AI system was found to be involved in any of this progress.
summary: The Gan-Gross-Prasad (GGP) conjecture, as Wikipedia's frozen bullet words it, is a broad restriction/period problem spanning real and p-adic Lie groups (orthogonal, unitary, GSpin, etc.), local and global versions, tempered and non-tempered representations. It is not a single yes/no statement, so no event fully resolves it; what counts under §3.1 is a genuine case (a restriction of the stated family), which several results since 26 January 2024 supply. The clearest is the Boisseau-Lu-Xue trilogy: part I (arXiv:2404.07342, submitted 10 April 2024) sets up the relative trace formula comparison for Fourier-Jacobi periods on unitary groups; part II (arXiv:2601.01727, posted 5/6 January 2026) compares the trace formulae; part III (arXiv:2601.01738, posted 5 January 2026) explicitly 'end[s] the proof of the conjectures via a reduction to the corank zero case' — completing a proof of the global GGP conjecture and its Ichino-Ikeda refinement for the Fourier-Jacobi-period case for unitary groups. This is a case of the stated problem (a restriction to a specific group type and period), settled entirely within the window, so I classify it `partial` with `resolution_direction` confirmed (the case came out as conjectured). A second, independent case was also settled in-window: Chen and Chen (arXiv:2507.04355, submitted 6 July 2025) prove the 'period implies relevance' direction of the non-tempered local GGP conjecture for Archimedean general linear groups, and state this, combined with a prior result of P. Boisseau on the converse direction, settles that whole sub-case ('this conjecture for general linear groups over Archimedean local fields is settled'). I did not independently verify Boisseau's converse-direction paper, so I treat this as strong secondary evidence for a settled case rather than as the primary event my status rests on; the Fourier-Jacobi trilogy alone is sufficient for `partial`. By contrast, the triage's first `found` item — the Springer 2024 publication of the (U(2n),U(1)) proof and its refinement — turns out to be `open_stale` material misdated by the triage: I confirmed via the arXiv abstract page (2205.09471) that version 1 was posted 19 May 2022, well before the frozen revision, and the 2024 Mathematische Annalen appearance is only the journal publication, which §6.3 explicitly says not to use for dating. I therefore treat that item as not contributing a new in-window event (though it doesn't change the overall `partial` status, since the Fourier-Jacobi case independently qualifies). The other two triage `found` items — the local twisted GL(V)/U(V) case (arXiv:2504.21002, Le, April 2025) and the GSpin Rankin-Selberg paper (arXiv:2508.09066, Yan, August 2025) — are genuine in-window preprints proving further cases/one-directions of local and global GGP respectively, reinforcing that this is an actively moving family of results, but neither is a full resolution and neither mentions AI. I searched extensively and specifically for any AI/LLM/AlphaEvolve/AlphaProof connection to GGP and found none: all identified authors are individual mathematicians (Boisseau, Lu, Xue, Chen, Chen, Le, Yan, Haan, Kwon) publishing conventional human-authored proofs, with no acknowledgement of AI assistance in any abstract, arXiv metadata, or accessible full text. The `ai_role` is therefore `none` across the board.
competing_reading: One could argue the Fourier-Jacobi-periods case and the Archimedean-GL non-tempered case are 'related problems' (variants defined over a different group/period type) rather than 'cases' of the single bullet 'Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture', in which case the correct status would be `open` with `no_change_found` true. I reject this reading because Wikipedia's own bullet describes GGP generically as 'a restriction problem in representation theory of real or p-adic Lie groups' without restricting to a particular group type, and the mathematical literature (including the papers themselves) treats these period/group-type specializations as cases of the single GGP conjecture, not as differently-posed problems — the trace-formula machinery and the conjectural framework (multiplicity formulas, Ichino-Ikeda refinements) is explicitly the same conjecture specialized to a subfamily of groups, matching §3.1's definition of a case as a restriction rather than a change of the question.
what_would_settle_it: A survey or expert digestion (e.g. a future ICM address, Bourbaki seminar, or Tao-style blog post) explicitly stating whether the Fourier-Jacobi trilogy and the Chen-Chen/Boisseau Archimedean-GL result are considered cases of 'the' Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture versus separate named results, would remove the ambiguity between 'case' and 'related problem' for this multi-strand conjecture family.
